Stack, integrations & measures

Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

Industry systems

What we integrate with.

Examples of systems commonly found in education. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

School and college ERP

Source of truth for admissions, attendance, timetables, fees, exams and student records. We read and write through its APIs or approved exports, and the ERP stays the system of record.

  • Entab CampusCare
  • Fedena
  • Teachmint
  • Samarth eGov for universities
  • MasterSoft

Learning platforms and LMS

Holds courses, assignments, progress and live session links. We use its events and APIs for homework digests, cohort reminders, progress nudges and analytics.

  • Google Classroom
  • Moodle
  • Canvas LMS
  • Graphy
  • In-house course apps

Coaching operations and assessment

Batch rosters, test responses and solved questions that feed batch scheduling, test analytics and doubt routing.

  • Classplus
  • Online test platforms
  • OMR scanning software
  • Question banks and solution libraries

Attendance and transport devices

Generate attendance and boarding events. We consume events from the vendor's interface, and location data stays within the transport system the school controls.

  • Biometric and RFID attendance
  • GPS bus trackers
  • Bus RFID card readers
  • Attendant mobile apps

National education platforms

Government rails for student identity, credits, verified documents and anti-ragging undertakings. We record IDs and reference numbers where families consent and the institution participates, and leave issuing to the official platforms.

  • UDISE+
  • APAAR and Academic Bank of Credits
  • DigiLocker
  • National Academic Depository
  • antiragging.in undertakings

Payments and accounting

Payment links, UPI, receipts and reconciliation against the ERP fee ledger, with GST invoices where a fee is taxable.

  • Razorpay
  • PayU
  • Easebuzz
  • Tally
  • Zoho Books

Messaging and telephony

Family channels with their own rules: opt-in and approved templates for WhatsApp, registered headers and templates for SMS, and preference checks for calls.

  • WhatsApp Business Platform via a solution provider
  • DLT-registered SMS gateway
  • Parent app push notifications
  • IVR or cloud telephony

Key measures

The KPIs we propose to track.

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

Enquiry first response time

Median time from a new admissions enquiry to the first meaningful reply by a counselor or approved automated message, split by staffed and unstaffed hours.

Why it matters: Families enquire with several institutions at once, and the first useful answer often decides who gets the visit.

Enquiry-to-enrollment conversion

Share of enquiries in a season that become confirmed admissions or paid enrollments, by source, program and campus.

Why it matters: Shows which channels and counseling practices actually fill seats, not just generate leads.

Media cost per confirmed admission

Media spend for a campaign divided by the confirmed admissions or enrollments attributed to it in the CRM, for the same season.

Why it matters: Moves marketing reviews from cost per lead to cost per seat filled.

Unexplained absence notification time

Time from the attendance cutoff to the parent being notified of an absence without approved leave, plus the share of unresolved cases phoned by staff the same day.

Why it matters: A child safety measure that parents and school leaders care about most.

Circular acknowledgment rate

Share of parents who acknowledged a circular that requires it, such as a trip consent slip, by its deadline.

Why it matters: Shows whether important notices are received and read, not just sent.

Teacher time on administration

Estimated weekly hours teachers and coordinators spend on substitution planning, parent messaging and report card handling, sampled before and after launch.

Why it matters: The purpose of staff-side automation is time returned to teaching and preparation.

On-time fee collection

Share of fee installments paid by the due date or within the grace period, by class, program or batch.

Why it matters: Tests whether private reminders and easy payment work without pressure on families or children.

Doubt resolution time

Median time from a doubt being submitted to an answer from the assigned faculty, by subject and batch.

Why it matters: Unanswered doubts are a common reason coaching and online learners fall behind.

Course completion rate

Share of enrolled learners who complete the required modules of a course or cohort within the planned period.

Why it matters: The core outcome for online learning and a strong driver of renewals and referrals.

Human handoff rate

Share of helpdesk conversations transferred to staff under the agreed rules, by reason such as grievance, sensitive message or low confidence.

Why it matters: Confirms sensitive matters reach people and shows where knowledge content needs work.

Integration principles

How we connect systems responsibly.

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
